D005-D007_h001.question:
I’m a robotics engineer, so I’m used to thinking in systems and probabilities, but what’s been happening the last two months doesn’t feel like a glitch I can debug.

For about eight weeks now, I’ve been convinced something catastrophic is coming—like everything is about to collapse. It’s not just climate change or the news; it feels certain, like I *know* the world is already in the process of ending, and everything around me is just running on borrowed time. It’s hard to shake, even when my wife tries to reason with me.

On top of that, I keep seeing things that I’m pretty sure aren’t really there—shadows moving in the room, people standing at the end of the hall who disappear when I look directly at them, sometimes these dark, cracked shapes on the walls, like the world is literally breaking apart. It happens at home and at work, even when I’m not especially upset.

I’ve had a few days here and there where I’ve felt really low—sad, drained, guilty about not being present with my wife—but those moods come and go. The strange beliefs and the things I see have been there pretty steadily, regardless of whether I feel depressed or not.
